title: Rollout orbital checks and rollback simulator
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, deterministic preflight harness (the 'orbital checks') and a rollback simulator that together provide fast, reproducible pass/fail signals for rollout gates. This ticket scopes an end-to-end prototype and the first automated pipeline integration for canary and staged rollouts.

Motivation: Existing preflight runs are heavy or slow to interpret: full eval suites take too long, smoke tests miss subtle perf degradations, and current rollback drills are manual. We need a middle-ground that is fast enough to run in preflight for each candidate build and expressive enough to catch regressions in latency, correctness heuristics, and cache-warm behaviors across runtime and quantized kernels.

What we'll deliver: 
- Orbital checks harness: a configurable runner that executes a small set (~10-20) of micro-scenarios designed to exercise upgrade-sensitive paths: cold-start latency, kv-cache warmstart/miss ratios, small/large-batch latency tails, streaming continuity, and quantized-vs-fp output deltas. Each scenario produces a fingerprint (latency distributions, token-level edit distance, and resource counters).
- Fast perf gates: statistical checks (median + 95th percentile deltas, and token-level correctness thresholds) that compute a rolling z-score against historical baseline. Failures categorize as latency, correctness, or resource regression.
- Rollback simulator: a deterministic dry-run that creates synthetic traffic bursts and injects capacity constraints to validate that automated rollback policies will be triggered and that fallbacks (model variants/regions) remain available. The simulator emits required signals to the rollout orchestrator.
- CI integration: a pipeline job that runs orbital checks on each release candidate in a canary namespace and posts a structured pass/fail verdict to the release orchestrator.
- Dashboard hooks: small dashboard tiles and logs that surface fingerprint diffs, top failing scenarios, and suggested mitigations (e.g., increase kv-cache warm pool, fallback to FP variant).

Acceptance criteria: 
1) Orbital checks runner implemented as a containerized job with stable config (yaml) and reproducible outputs.
2) Perf gates detect injected 15% median latency regressions and 30% 95th-tail regressions in controlled tests.
3) Correctness gate detects a 1.5% token-level edit-distance increase in targeted evals.
4) Rollback simulator triggers the same automated rollback path that we use in staged rollouts in our canary env.
5) CI job created and invoked in canary pipeline; PR link included in comments.

Non-goals: This ticket is NOT the full long-form eval suite or the final production rollout UI. It focuses on a fast, deterministic signal for release gating.
comments: 2026-02-26: Kickoff — scoped scenarios with runtime, perf, and platform teams. Decided to avoid full-batch reproducibility; instead we will focus on distributional fingerprints.

2026-03-02: Design review — feedback from Runtime (J. Patel): include quantized kernel warmup and a KV cache hit-rate sweep. Action: add a dedicated scenario that seeds KV cache and measures cold vs warm latencies.

2026-03-05: PoC runner completed (local). Includes 5 scenarios: cold-start, kv-warm, micro-batch tail, streaming-resume, and quantized-delta. PoC output schema: csv + json summary (latency hist, token-diffs, resource counters).
2026-03-07: Integration PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1289 — CI job definition + container image. Added reviewer: @anika-s.

2026-03-09: First synthetic injection tests — perf gates caught a 20% median latency reg when we throttled GPU clocks. Rollback simulator exercised fallback to model-variant successfully in canary namespace. Need to harden noise thresholds.
2026-03-10: Planning next: add automatic baseline selection (last green release) and implement z-score smoothing to reduce false positives during noisy windows.
notes: Keep scenarios minimal and deterministic. Avoid any heavy offline eval data that would slow CI. If a scenario requires >2 minutes to run, split or rework it. Use small synthetic datasets that mimic production token distributions.
observability_requirements: Emit scenario_name, timestamp, median_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, token_edit_rate, kv_hit_rate, cpu_pct, gpu_mem_mb as top-level metrics. Post JSON fingerprint artifact to S3-like store for deeper analysis.
implementation_plan: Week 1: finalize scenarios and PoC harness. Week 2: implement perf gates and rollback simulator. Week 3: CI integration and dashboard hook. Week 4: run on 3 canary RCs and tune thresholds.
mitigations: Fail open for first 2 weeks in non-critical rollouts
Iterate scenarios with runtime and product to improve coverage
